 REPRESENTED BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR,HIGH COURT OF  KERALA, PIN - 682031  THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 16.11.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2 B.A No. 9323 of 2023  ORDER
This is an application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking regular bail.
2. The petitioner is the accused in Crime No. 486/2022 of Devikulam Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 376, 376 (2) (n), 376 AB and 506 of Indian Penal Code read with Section 3(a), 4, 5i, 5l, 5m, 6 of POCSO Act.

The allegation against the petitioner is that, during the Onam holidays in the year 2022, the petitioner trespassed into the house of the victim, who was a neighbour and a girl aged 7 years,
committed rape on her.
The crime was registered in such circumstances and as part of the investigation the petitioner was arrested on 27.10.2022.
Since then, he has been under judicial detention.

Even though the petitioner had approached this Court on an earlier occasion, by filing B.A No. 4994/2023, the same culminated in Annexure A1 order by which the said application was dismissed taking note of the serious nature of allegations.
This is the second application submitted by him seeking regular bail.
4. Heard, Sri. Abhilash J, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Jacob E Simon, the learned Public Prosecutor, appearing for the State.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner was falsely implicated in the said case and it was further pointed out that, he has been under judicial detention for more than one year.
He is a person aged 63 years suffering from various ailments including cardiac problems.
The petitioner requires urgent medical attention.
Besides the same, it is pointed out that, even though the trial has commenced and 17 witnesses were examined, the trial could not be proceeded further for want of FSL report.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor on the other hand opposes the said contention by highlighting the serious nature of allegations and the tender age of the victim.
It was pointed out that the chances of influencing the victim are very high and therefore, bail cannot be granted.
With regard to the FSL report, the learned Public Prosecutor points out that, the same has not been received so far.
He confirmed that the petitioner is having certain physical ailments which require medical treatment.
The learned Public Prosecutor made available the certificate issued from the Medical College Hospital, Kottayam, showing the necessity of the treatment of the petitioner.
7. I have carefully gone through the records.
Of course it is true that, there are serious allegations raised against the petitioner.
At the same time, the right of a speedy trial of the accused is also a matter which is to be taken into consideration.

Earlier when the matter came up for consideration, a report was called for from the Fast Track Special Court, Devikulam as to the present status of S.C No. 729/2022 and the probable time that may be required to complete the trial of the said case in the normal circumstances.

8. In response to the same, a report dated 13.11.2023 has been placed on record by the learned Judge, wherein, it is mentioned that, even though 27 witnesses were cited only 17 of the witnesses could be examined and to complete the trial, the FSL report is necessary.
It was also pointed out that the trial can be completed within a period of two months after obtaining the FSL report.
Thus there is some uncertainty as to the period within which the trial can be completed.
It is an admitted position that the petitioner requires medical attention.
The petitioner is also a person 63 years, and he does not have any criminal antecedents as well.

In such circumstances, considering the age of the petitioner, and his physical condition which requires medical attention, long period of incarceration the petitioner had already undergone, and Xxx vs State Of Kerala on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183143916/
2 other relevant circumstances, I deem it appropriate to grant bail to the petitioner subject to stringent conditions.

Thus, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on the following conditions:-
i) The petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs. 1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
ii) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
iii) The petitioner shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.
iv) The petitioner shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
v) The petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the trial Court.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.
